hypotheses.justification: The theorem only takes this instance because its variables K and L appear in the statement; there is no `omit`. `retr` is a `def`, and Lean's `withUsed` (Lean/Elab/MutualDef.lean, around line 1421) drops section variables that definitions do not use, so `retr` does not take `FiniteDimensional`. Its body (`TensorProduct.lid`, `LinearMap.rTensor`, the right-action A-module structure on L ⊗[K] A) needs only Field K, Field L, Algebra K L, CommRing A and Algebra K A. The proof (`show` unfolding retr, then `rw [LinearMap.rTensor_tmul, TensorProduct.lid_tmul]`) never uses finite-dimensionality, so the identity holds for any K-algebra L and `omit [FiniteDimensional K L] in` leaves the proof unchanged.

This instance is included only because A appears in the statement. Neither `retr`, which as a `def` takes only the variables it uses, nor the rewriting proof with `LinearMap.rTensor_tmul` and `TensorProduct.lid_tmul` involves any topology. The statement is a purely algebraic identity about tensors, so it stays true and provable with the same proof once this instance is omitted. ([TopologicalSpace A] is also unused, but it cannot be deleted alone because the type of [IsTopologicalRing A] mentions it.)
